- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2bcaefba91b746c1a43066352b5bd4d319519c35` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `66729872a8250fe18c24d18c201f25a4df29a1f0` — the merge of head `292bf5f32866179767f547fc8ffee0877d17597c` into base `2bcaefba91b746c1a43066352b5bd4d319519c35`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 66729872a8250fe18c24d18c201f25a4df29a1f0 && git checkout 66729872a8250fe18c24d18c201f25a4df29a1f0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2bcaefba91b746c1a43066352b5bd4d319519c35 292bf5f32866179767f547fc8ffee0877d17597c && git checkout -B drift-repro 2bcaefba91b746c1a43066352b5bd4d319519c35 && git merge --no-ff 292bf5f32866179767f547fc8ffee0877d17597c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2bcaefba91b746c1a43066352b5bd4d319519c35
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2bcaefba91b746c1a43066352b5bd4d319519c35` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `890c170d5097f82d3b2ed310b27e393fc554d6fd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts + packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.test.ts, .changeset/24165-mcp-token-organization-id.md, content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/spec/src/security/tenancy-posture.ts, packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.mcp-oauth-resource.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts, docs/adr/0090-permission-model-v2-concept-convergence.md, docs/adr/0123-no-active-organization-session-semantics.md

**Head note.** The brief named `06210ccf8f233f8e8c71df861a3d7808795a9546`. While this review was being read the branch gained one commit (16:11:30Z, `890c170d5`, a 4-line restatement of the same contract on `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`), so the PR's head moved. Both heads were read in full: the net diff of `890c170d5` against `origin/main` (`2bcaefba9`, merge-base `cb8756b00`) is the briefed three files plus that docs page, 4 files, +63/-3; `main` has not touched `packages/spec/src/contracts/` since the base. This record names the head that can land. Inputs were card #24165 (body and both comments), parent #24137 (body and all six comments, ruling `6232069920`), PR #24189 (body, file list, net diff), and the check-runs on both heads; nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Public surface — RIGHT.** `IAuthService.verifyMcpAccessToken`'s result type gains `organizationId?: string`: optional and additive, so every existing implementer still satisfies the contract; an interface member, so no emitted JavaScript changes; no export is added, so the `api-surface` shard does not move and the diff carries no generated artifact. `Type Check · source gates` (green on both heads) ran `check:generated --reconcile-only` and `check:docs`; `check:api-surface` rides `Type Check · consumer gates` (see the check-run note in ③).
2. **Member semantics against ruling `6232069920` — RIGHT.** Item 1: "the organization the user's OAuth consent bound … read from the access token's `organization_id` claim" is the ruling's binding and claim name verbatim. Item 2: "vetted on every request by `vetOrganizationClaim`" names the session arm's rule (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:704-720`, which drops an unbacked claim and re-resolves with no tenant; the API-key arm at `:622-640` refuses instead), and the TSDoc states the session arm's consequence, which is what sub-question 2 (a) chose; "never the union of the user's organizations" and "never the organization the user's browser session has selected now" restate the ruling's two negatives. Item 3: "no organization, global grants only, tenant reads come back empty and tenant writes are refused" is ADR-0123 D2 as written. "Under ADR-0090 D10 it is the organization the delegator's grants are resolved in" does not restate D10 (D10 fixes the intersection and names no organization); it states what this member supplies to it, which is the card's finding and the ruling's purpose. No new claim, column or stored field beyond the one member.
3. **The `client_credentials` sentence — WRONG.** The TSDoc says the member is "absent when no consent bound one: a token minted before consents bound an organization, and a machine-to-machine (`client_credentials`) token, which no user consented to", and the test comment spells it as "a client_credentials token, verify with none". The one implementer refuses such a token before any result exists: `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts:6786-6837` answers `null` when `sub` equals `client_id` or `azp` ("A `client_credentials` (M2M) token is REFUSED here — the MCP surface is principal-bound by design; headless callers use API keys"), and that refusal is pinned against a real minted token (`auth-manager.mcp-oauth-resource.test.ts`, docblock item 5). Core's `OAuthTokenProvenance.userId` (`assemble-execution-context.ts:181`) is "the human `sub` the token was issued for". So an M2M token never reaches the result this member sits on; the sentence describes an absence on a result the surface refuses by design, and a reader of the contract — the `plugin-auth` seat implementing #24166 reads this TSDoc as the member's spec — concludes that a `client_credentials` token verifies on MCP with no organization, which is exactly the admission the real-token pin closed. The ruling names no M2M case; the wording is the card body's gloss. It now stands on four carriers: the TSDoc, the test comment, the changeset body (which ships as `CHANGELOG.md` and is release-owned afterwards), and the docs page line added by `890c170d5`. A claim no wider than the enforcement is the rule (Prime Directive 10); this is the one defect of the diff.
4. **The pin — RIGHT.** Two typed reads (`string | undefined`) off a bound and an unbound result, in the interface's existing test home; `packages/spec/test-typecheck-debt.json` carries no entry for `auth-service.test.ts`, so `check:test-typecheck` compiles it with zero ledger debt and the dev's ablation (deleting the member reds that gate) is the right shape for a type-only member.
5. **Precision note, not a defect.** "Once no current membership backs it, the principal resolves with no organization" holds under the walled postures; under `single`, `vetOrganizationClaim` returns the claim unvetted (`postureEnforcesWall` is false for `single` alone, `tenancy-posture.ts:53`), exactly as it does for a REST session's claim. The TSDoc names the rule rather than re-spelling it, so the simplification is the ruling's own.
6. **Hand-copied shapes left as they are — RIGHT.** The runtime's local `oauthPrincipal` type (`resolve-execution-context.ts:146`), core's `OAuthTokenProvenance` (`:181`) and the implementer's return type (`auth-manager.ts:6788`) still spell the three-member shape; the member is optional, so nothing breaks, and all three sit in the dispatch's hold-offs and the runtime slice (#24137) extends them. The implementer answering `null` where the contract says `undefined` is pre-existing and dormant, as the acceptance note says.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` `minor` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the changeset and `Clause-②: yes` on the PR body — RIGHT. Both read as `yes` and not breaking by the fleet's one reader (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`; the `widening` arm reads as not breaking in `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`), and the double-carrier discipline was retired by ruling record 5770886272, so the spelling difference is not a defect. `yes` takes at least `minor`: met. No `skip-changeset`; nothing is removed or renamed, so no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. `Check Changeset` is green on both heads. The changeset body carries the `client_credentials` clause of ①.3 and takes the same trim; once released, that text can only be amended by a dedicated docs PR.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none declared by the dev; none found.
- Dev deviations, each answered: `main` was not merged before the PR opened — the net diff against current `origin/main` is unchanged and `main` has not moved `packages/spec/src/contracts/` since the base, and the queue re-verifies on its rebuilt generation; the shallow-root fetch of a fixture commit is a read; the commit trailers follow AGENTS.md; the Clause-② spellings are answered in ②; the stopped mis-typed vitest run has no bearing on the contract.
- **Flag, escalated to the owning seat:** commit `890c170d5` edits `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`, a path under the dispatch claim's `content/docs/**` hold-off (`6234980714`: "stop on a breach and explain it in the report"), pushed four minutes after the os-dev-report that declared the work done, with no stop and no explanation on the card. The prompt was the advisory Docs Drift comment (`6236317366`), not a gate (`scripts/docs-audit/handwritten-docs.json` is a ledger of hand-written pages, nothing reds on that page). The edit itself keeps the page in step with the contract. The seat decides whether the page edit stays in this PR or moves to the lane the hold-off reserved it for; if it stays, its new line carries the same trim as ①.3.
- Out-of-scope finding (runtime's stale "implemented and undeclared" comment at `resolve-execution-context.ts:154`, and its local type): carrier #24137, agreed; not this slice's file.
- **Check-runs, recorded as read.** On `06210ccf8`: 24 success, 6 skipped, 10 cancelled, 1 failure. Both heavy runs (`CI` 39047887346, `Lint & Type Check` 39047887379) were cancelled mid-build at 16:12Z by the 16:11Z push (`cancel-in-progress` on both workflows' PR-keyed concurrency group); every cancelled step is a build or test step, and the one `failure`, `TypeScript Type Check`, is its "Verify every type-check lane succeeded" aggregate reporting the cancelled lanes, not a content failure. On `890c170d5` at the time of this record (16:23Z): 26 success, 5 skipped, 8 in progress (Test Core 1 to 6, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates); `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · source gates` and `Type Check · debt ledger` are green. Their conclusions are theirs; this record does not wait on them.

**What PASS needs:** drop the `client_credentials` / machine-to-machine clause from the four carriers (TSDoc, test comment, changeset body, docs line), keeping "absent for a token minted before consents bound an organization"; if the M2M case is worth a word, say that such a token is refused before this result is reached, as the implementer does. A new head takes a new record.
